factual_issues.where: git-commit / reseed; speech starting “See? The older lines”; D historical commit messages
factual_issues.claim: c04a049 is ReSeed's first commit, and the displayed older commits are real ReSeed history.
factual_issues.problem: E supplies no Git history confirming commit IDs, their order, or their messages. These details should not be presented as verified ReSeed history.
factual_issues.evidence: E contains excerpts headed “.github/workflows/tests.yml”, “.github/workflows/pages.yml”, and “README.md (The website)”, but no commit log.
factual_issues.fix: This garden shows example commits: a first version, new ideas, and bug fixes. To explore ReSeed's actual saved history, use `git log --oneline`.

factual_issues.claim: node tests/js/forestnet.test.mjs checks that JavaScript ForestNet gives the same answers as PyTorch.
factual_issues.problem: The workflow confirms that this test file runs, but E does not show what it checks. Its filename alone does not establish a comparison with PyTorch.
factual_issues.evidence: tests.yml: “- run: node tests/js/forestnet.test.mjs”. README: “the real network in plain JavaScript”. Neither excerpt describes the test assertions.
factual_issues.fix: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` sets up Python 3.12 and Node 22, runs `python -m pytest -q`, then runs `node tests/js/forestnet.test.mjs` to test the JavaScript ForestNet code.

general_cs_errors.where: speech and D starting “Every save plants a tree”
general_cs_errors.claim: Every save creates a commit, runs tests, and publishes the website.
general_cs_errors.problem: Saving a file is not committing it. Local commits also do not automatically trigger these GitHub workflows; pushing is a separate step.
general_cs_errors.fix: Every commit plants a tree. Push to main, and robots test the code and publish the website!

general_cs_errors.where: ci-tests / text; speech starting “Send it with git push”
general_cs_errors.claim: GitHub Actions runs tests on every push, and red means something broke.
general_cs_errors.problem: Actions only runs tests when a workflow is configured to do so. A failed run can also result from setup or service problems, rather than broken application code.
general_cs_errors.fix: **GitHub Actions** can run tests when you push. ReSeed sets this up! Green ✓ means the checks passed; red ✗ means a check failed. (Game version: the NDVI bug here is pretend.)

general_cs_errors.claim: -am puts changed files in the basket and commits.
general_cs_errors.problem: git commit -am stages changes only to already tracked files. It does not include new, untracked files.
general_cs_errors.fix: Save the fix: `-am` adds changes to files Git already tracks, then commits.
